RÉEXAMINÉE le 2026-09-03 après ldpy 0.6.3 (fiche ldpy/027) et MAINTENUE not-expressible. `as` la rendrait syntaxiquement traduisible — `@prefix entity: f<{namespace_prefix}entity/> as _e .` puis `self.entity_namespace = _e` — mais ce serait FORCER : deux lignes au lieu d'une, sans qu'un seul nom préfixé `entity:` soit écrit dans la région. La construction n'y gagne rien, donc elle ne s'y crédite pas. C'est un point de mesure utile : `as` lève la limite là où l'objet DOIT survivre ET où le préfixe sert aussi lexicalement, pas partout où un Namespace est construit. Les deux autres namespaces de la région sont des PARAMÈTRES reçus, que rien ne déclare ici.

[note antérieure] not-expressible, and a genuine finding, not a shortcut: NEITHER namespace this region touches is ever DEREFERENCED as a term (`NS.something`) within this region's own body -- `NGSILD` (from lib.utils, verified as a real `Namespace('https://uri.etsi.org/ngsi-ld/')` in utils.py line 85) is only assigned to `self.ngsildns`; `self.entity_namespace = Namespace(f'{namespace_prefix}entity/')` builds a namespace at runtime from a per-instance value. Both are stored as opaque Namespace OBJECTS on `self` purely so a SIBLING method can dereference them later -- verified directly against the pinned commit: entity.py line 90, `Entity.set_attribute`, reads `self.entity_namespace[attributename]`, NOT part of this extracted region. Why no island covers this: `from … import p:` and `@prefix … f<…>` (declarations.md) both declare a prefix LEXICALLY, scoped to the block that declares it -- neither produces a runtime value that could be assigned to `self.X` for a different method to read later. Converting `NGSILD` to a prefix import removes it as a plain Python name entirely (declarations.md: 'no name is captured'), breaking `self.ngsildns = NGSILD`; converting the dynamic `Namespace(f'{namespace_prefix}entity/')` to `@prefix uaentity: f<{namespace_prefix}entity/> .` would make `self.entity_namespace` unavailable to `set_attribute`, a method this region does not include and which the study forbids restructuring (INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2: no refactorisation). This is the ns_import_project stratum meeting a shape real code actually has -- a namespace threaded across methods via an instance attribute, not dereferenced at its own construction site -- rather than a limit already catalogued in INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS5. The region's remaining operations (`Graph()`, two `.bind()` calls, a list literal) are graph/namespace-manager BOOKKEEPING, not triples: no `g{ }`/`+{ }`/`m{ }` island targets a bare `Graph()` construction or a namespace-manager `.bind()` (the SS2 correspondence table has no row for either), so `constructions` is genuinely empty rather than under-reported. translated.ldpy is therefore byte-identical Python to original.py's own region body (both import lines rewritten identically to the executability shim, see below) -- the pair still proves nothing broke, and the driver exercises it for real: list(self.e) (empty, no triples added by __init__), the two namespace bindings, str(self.entity_namespace), str(self.ngsildns), basens, opcuans, types. Executability (AGENT_BATCH's 163-regions case): `lib.utils` (a real dotted project path that cannot resolve for a single extracted file) rewritten to `lib_utils_context`, a shim module transcribing NGSILD verbatim; collection_to_list/calculate_array_dimensions are imported by the real file's own context line but never called by this region -- left as raise-if-invoked placeholders rather than transcribing utils.py lines 118-150+ (which read a datagraph this region never builds), not reached by this region. demo(namespace_prefix, basens, opcuans) (identical on both sides, appended after the region) builds a plain `_Blank()` self and returns the region's writable results, not `self` itself: a plain object has no __eq__ and the harness's per-argument comparison always reports 'values differ' by identity otherwise -- same failure mode and same fix as the acdh-oeaw/vocabseditor and DataDrivenCPS/acquirium siblings of this stratum.
